positions.stance: "A judge's role is to apply the law fairly and impartially."
Committed to "upholding the United States and Texas Constitutions."
Committed to "applying statutes and binding precedent as written."
Committed to "ensuring that all litigants receive due process."
Committed to "treating every person with dignity and respect in the courtroom."

tx-tarrant-2026-county-judge-o-hare-tim.name: Tim O'Hare
tx-tarrant-2026-county-judge-o-hare-tim.bio: Tarrant County Judge; former Mayor of Farmers Branch and attorney who built a law firm and real estate business.

positions.stance: Says he delivered the largest property tax cuts in county history and adopted tax rates below the no-new-revenue rate four years in a row.
Says he cut over $70 million from the operating budget, halted "pork capital projects," and tightened county travel policies.
Cites historic pay raises for law enforcement and funded task forces on cold cases, human trafficking, drug dealers, and auto theft.
Advocates "a return to common-sense governance that respects faith, freedom, and family values."
Championed election reforms including improved ballot chain-of-custody and elimination of internet-based results transmission.

tx-tarrant-2026-county-judge-simmons-ali.name: Alisa Simmons
tx-tarrant-2026-county-judge-simmons-ali.bio: Tarrant County Commissioner since 2022; former president of the Arlington NAACP, newsroom journalist, 9-1-1 public safety leader, and entrepreneur.

positions.stance: Plans to expand youth mental health support, strengthen early intervention, and divert people with mental health needs away from the justice system.
Proposes independent investigation, automatic medical review, family notification, and public disclosure after any death in county jail custody.
Calls for "real fiscal responsibility at Commissioners Court" and criticizes recent county budget decisions, including use of reserves.

tx-tarrant-2026-ccl3-hrabal-mike.name: Mike Hrabal
tx-tarrant-2026-ccl3-hrabal-mike.bio: Judge of Tarrant County Court at Law No. 3.

positions.stance: Believes judges decide disputes rather than make law; adheres to an originalist interpretation and "strict construction" of the Constitution.
Says existing law should be enforced against lawyers who file frivolous lawsuits or litigate abusively.
Does not allow special interest groups to influence his judgment; every litigant is treated "with dignity, respect and fairness."
Aims to ensure the justice system "remains accessible, expedient and even-handed."
Believes a County Court at Law must provide "expedient, economical, informed, and predictable justice to all Texans."

tx-tarrant-2026-ccc4-nekhom-deborah.name: Deborah Nekhom
tx-tarrant-2026-ccc4-nekhom-deborah.bio: Judge of Tarrant County Criminal Court No. 4 since 2003.

tx-tarrant-2026-ccc5-clark-brad.name: Brad Clark
tx-tarrant-2026-ccc5-clark-brad.bio: Presiding judge of Tarrant County Criminal Court No. 5 with over 30 years of criminal law experience as a prosecutor, defense attorney, and small business owner.

tx-tarrant-2026-ccc5-billhymer-julya.name: Julya "Jujubill" Billhymer
tx-tarrant-2026-ccc5-billhymer-julya.bio: Criminal defense attorney for 27 years and former patrol sergeant in Tarrant and Dallas counties.

tx-tarrant-2026-ccc6-hartin-randi.name: Randi Hartin
tx-tarrant-2026-ccc6-hartin-randi.bio: Judge of Tarrant County Criminal Court No. 6 since 2022; former prosecutor, criminal defense and family law attorney, and public school teacher.

tx-tarrant-2026-ccc7-starnes-eric.name: Eric Starnes
tx-tarrant-2026-ccc7-starnes-eric.bio: Elected Judge of Tarrant County Criminal Court No. 7.

tx-tarrant-2026-ccc8-vanover-charles.name: Charles L. "Chuck" Vanover
tx-tarrant-2026-ccc8-vanover-charles.bio: Judge of Tarrant County Criminal Court No. 8; former police officer and Tarrant County prosecutor.

tx-tarrant-2026-ccc9-bolton-brian.name: Brian Bolton
tx-tarrant-2026-ccc9-bolton-brian.bio: Judge of Tarrant County Criminal Court No. 9 since 2022; former chief prosecutor and defense attorney.

tx-tarrant-2026-ccc9-pamplin-lesa.name: Lesa Pamplin
tx-tarrant-2026-ccc9-pamplin-lesa.bio: Attorney with 34 years in the justice system as a police officer, prosecutor, and defense attorney.

positions.stance: "Unwavering and impartial justice for every citizen, in every case"; pledges to set aside personal biases and follow the law consistently.
Decisions based on "the law and the facts, not on political pressure, public opinion, or personal gain"; follows the Constitution and respects precedent.
"Justice you can see and trust"; pledges open proceedings, clearly explained decisions, and accountability to the community.

tx-tarrant-2026-ccc10-loftin-trent.name: Trent Loftin
tx-tarrant-2026-ccc10-loftin-trent.bio: Attorney practicing criminal defense, juvenile, probation violation, and divorce cases.

tx-tarrant-2026-probate1-burns-patricia.name: Patricia Burns
tx-tarrant-2026-probate1-burns-patricia.bio: Judge who practiced probate, guardianship, mental health, and civil litigation for over 25 years before taking the bench.

tx-tarrant-2026-probate2-bell-brook.name: Brook Bell
tx-tarrant-2026-probate2-bell-brook.bio: Associate Judge of Tarrant County Probate Court No. 2 and Texas A&M University School of Law professor.

tx-williamson-2026-county-judge-snell-st.name: Steve Snell
tx-williamson-2026-county-judge-snell-st.bio: Williamson County Judge since April 2025; former public school superintendent, including of Liberty Hill ISD.

positions.stance: Will focus on "Lower County Property Tax Rates."
Will "Properly Fund Our Sheriff & First Responders."
Will work to "Open a Regional Medical Examiner's Office."
Will "Support Small Business & Grow Our County Economy to Reduce Homeowner Taxes."
Supports "Smart Road Plans That Protect Our Quality of Life."

tx-williamson-2026-county-judge-jefts-he.name: Heather Jefts
tx-williamson-2026-county-judge-jefts-he.bio: Small business owner and four-term member of the Cedar Park City Council.

positions.stance: Pledges to remain available through office hours and to respond to letters, emails, and phone calls.
Calls safety her "highest priority"; will work with EMS, the Sheriff, Constables, and others to ensure they have needed tools and training.
Says it is "critical we balance public safety and infrastructure needs with efficient and responsible government spending."
Committed to "championing solutions that address safety, air quality, and congestion."
Committed to "supporting great businesses that provide quality jobs" and keeping the economy diverse.

tx-williamson-2026-coa3-chief-liu-cory.name: Cory Liu
tx-williamson-2026-coa3-chief-liu-cory.bio: Judge of the 250th District Court in Travis County; former law firm attorney and Assistant General Counsel in the Office of the Governor.

tx-williamson-2026-coa3-chief-byrne-darl.name: Darlene Byrne
tx-williamson-2026-coa3-chief-byrne-darl.bio: Chief Justice of the Third Court of Appeals, elected to the court in 2020; previously presiding judge of Travis County's 126th District Court for 20 years.

positions.stance: Believes "time is of the essence when making decisions that impact the lives of real Texans," so justice is not delayed.

tx-williamson-2026-dj368-bruchmiller-sar.name: Sarah Bruchmiller
tx-williamson-2026-dj368-bruchmiller-sar.bio: District Judge of the 368th District Court of Williamson County; former prosecutor.

tx-williamson-2026-dj512-moore-sarah.name: Sarah Moore
tx-williamson-2026-dj512-moore-sarah.bio: Judge of the 512th District Court since a March 2026 appointment; career prosecutor and Board-Certified attorney.

tx-williamson-2026-dj512-booker-leslie.name: Leslie Booker
tx-williamson-2026-dj512-booker-leslie.bio: Attorney with over thirty years of experience who leads her own law firm; former public defender and prosecutor.

tx-williamson-2026-ccl1-hallford-brandy.name: Brandy Hallford
tx-williamson-2026-ccl1-hallford-brandy.bio: Judge of Williamson County Court at Law No. 1; former prosecutor for Williamson County, Dallas County, and the Texas Attorney General's Office.
